27:                 upper = min(sz2, i + width) + 1
28:                 mask[i, lower:upper] = True
29:         return mask
30:     if backend is numpy:
31:         return njit(nogil=True)(_sakoe_chiba_mask_generic)
32:     else:
33:         return _sakoe_chiba_mask_generic
34: 
35: _njit_sakoe_chiba_mask = __make_sakoe_chiba_mask(numpy)
36: if HAS_TORCH:
37:     _sakoe_chiba_mask = __make_sakoe_chiba_mask(instantiate_backend("torch"))
38: else:
39:     _sakoe_chiba_mask = _njit_sakoe_chiba_mask
40: 
41: 
42: def sakoe_chiba_mask(sz1, sz2, radius=1, be=None):
43:     """Compute the Sakoe-Chiba mask.
44: 
45:     Parameters
46:     ----------
47:     sz1 : int
48:         The size of the first time series
49:     sz2 : int
50:         The size of the second time series.
51:     radius : int
52:         The radius of the band.
53:     be : Backend object or string or None
54:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
55:         the NumPy backend is used.
56:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
57:         the PyTorch backend is used.
58:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
59:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
60: 
61:     Returns
62:     -------
63:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
64:         Sakoe-Chiba mask.
65: 
66:     Examples
67:     --------
68:     >>> sakoe_chiba_mask(4, 4, radius=2)
69:     array([[ True,  True,  True, False],
70:            [ True,  True,  True,  True],
71:            [ True,  True,  True,  True],
72:            [False,  True,  True,  True]])
73:     """
74:     be = instantiate_backend(be)
75:     if be.is_numpy:
76:         return _njit_sakoe_chiba_mask(
77:             sz1,
78:             sz2,
79:             radius,
80:         )
81:     else:
82:         return _sakoe_chiba_mask(
83:             sz1,
84:             sz2,
85:             radius,
86:         )
87: 
88: 
89: def __make_itakura_mask(backend):
90: 
91:     def _itakura_mask_generic(sz1, sz2, max_slope=2.0):
92:         min_slope = 1 / float(max_slope)
93:         max_slope *= float(sz1) / float(sz2)
94:         min_slope *= float(sz1) / float(sz2)
95: 
96:         lower_bound = backend.empty((2, sz2))
97:         lower_bound[0] = min_slope * backend.arange(sz2)
98:         lower_bound[1] = (sz1 - 1) - max_slope * (sz2 - 1) + max_slope * backend.arange(sz2)
99:         lower_bound_ = backend.empty(sz2)
100:         for i in range(sz2):
101:             lower_bound_[i] = max(
102:                 backend.round(lower_bound[0, i], decimals=2),
103:                 backend.round(lower_bound[1, i], decimals=2)
104:             )
105:         lower_bound_ = backend.ceil(lower_bound_)
106: 
107:         upper_bound = backend.empty((2, sz2))
108:         upper_bound[0] = max_slope * backend.arange(sz2)
109:         upper_bound[1] = (sz1 - 1) - min_slope * (sz2 - 1) + min_slope * backend.arange(sz2)
110:         upper_bound_ = backend.empty(sz2)
111:         for i in range(sz2):
112:             upper_bound_[i] = min(
113:                 backend.round(upper_bound[0, i], decimals=2),
114:                 backend.round(upper_bound[1, i], decimals=2)
115:             )
116:         upper_bound_ = backend.floor(upper_bound_ + 1)
117: 
118:         mask = backend.full((sz1, sz2), False)
119:         for i in range(sz2):
120:             mask[int(lower_bound_[i]): int(upper_bound_[i]), i] = True
121: 
122:         # Post-check
123:         raise_warning = False
124:         for i in range(sz1):
125:             if not backend.any(mask[i]):
126:                 raise_warning = True
127:                 break
128:         if not raise_warning:
129:             for j in range(sz2):
130:                 if not backend.any(mask[:, j]):
131:                     raise_warning = True
132:                     break
133:         if raise_warning:
134:             raise RuntimeWarning(
135:                 "'itakura_max_slope' constraint is unfeasible "
136:                 "(ie. leads to no admissible path) for the "
137:                 "provided time series sizes",
138:             )
139: 
140:         return mask
141: 
142:     if backend is numpy:
143:         return njit(nogil=True)(_itakura_mask_generic)
144:     else:
145:         return _itakura_mask_generic
146: 
147: _njit_itakura_mask = __make_itakura_mask(numpy)
148: if HAS_TORCH:
149:     _itakura_mask = __make_itakura_mask(instantiate_backend("torch"))
150: else:
151:     _itakura_mask = _njit_itakura_mask
152: 
153: 
154: def itakura_mask(sz1, sz2, max_slope=2.0, be=None):
155:     """Compute the Itakura mask.
156: 
157:     Parameters
158:     ----------
159:     sz1 : int
160:         The size of the first time series
161:     sz2 : int
162:         The size of the second time series.
163:     max_slope : float (default = 2)
164:         The maximum slope of the parallelogram.
165:     be : Backend object or string or None
166:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
167:         the NumPy backend is used.
168:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
169:         the PyTorch backend is used.
170:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
171:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
172: 
173:     Returns
174:     -------
175:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
176:         Itakura mask.
177: 
178:     Examples
179:     --------
180:     >>> itakura_mask(6, 6, max_slope=3)
181:     array([[ True, False, False, False, False, False],
182:            [False,  True,  True,  True, False, False],
